1:1.t: The second year of Darius I of Persia was 520 BC. The sixth month began on August 29. The exiles had returned in 538 BC, laid the temple foundation, and then stopped work for sixteen years (Ezra 3-5).

2:16.t: "Measures": the Hebrew does not name the unit.

1:5.t: "Give careful thought to your ways" (Hebrew simu levavkhem al darkhekhem): literally "set your heart on your ways". The people's hardships were a call to put God first.

1:7.t: "Give careful thought to your ways" (Hebrew simu levavkhem al darkhekhem): literally "set your heart on your ways". The people's hardships were a call to put God first.

2:7.t: "The desire of all nations will come": the KJV's reading, which has long been understood of the Messiah. The Hebrew chemdat (singular) with a plural verb may also mean "the treasures of all nations will come", as verse 8 suggests.

2:9.t: "The glory of this latter house will be greater than the glory of the former": the rebuilt temple was smaller, but Jesus would teach in its courts. Hebrews 12:26-28 quotes verse 6 of the final shaking that leaves only God's unshakable kingdom.

2:23.t: "Like My signet ring": a reversal of the curse on Zerubbabel's grandfather Jehoiachin (Jeremiah 22:24). Zerubbabel, of David's line, is an ancestor of Jesus (Matthew 1:12-13).
